title: Stochastic session-weighted billing allocator
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: As request fanout and multi-model routing increased, deterministic last-writer attribution for short-lived sessions produced noisy refunds and unfair credits for customers using parallel routes (canary + fallback). Late-arriving tokens (edge bursts, retries) and partial-success responses made per-request token attribution brittle. Current ledger approach creates spikes and retroactive adjustments that cascade to downstream billing jobs.

Goal: Implement a probabilistic/stochastic allocator that assigns fractional token credits across concurrent session shards using session confidence weights and adaptive smoothing. The design should reduce retroactive invoice churn, distribute late-arrival tokens proportionally to likely originators, and be idempotent for replayed/duplicate events. It must integrate with existing streaming ingestion (Kafka->Beam), be compatible with token ledger snapshots, and expose explainability traces in Console.

Scope: This ticket implements the allocator microservice and ingestion transforms. It includes: (1) heuristic/session-confidence calculators (route success rate, model-latency, tenant-priority), (2) reservoir-based sampler for burst smoothing, (3) Bayesian smoothing layer to avoid zero-probability allocations, (4) a compact attribution event schema for downstream billing joins, and (5) rollout plan with shadow and canary modes. Not included: final invoice presentation UI (separate PM ticket).
acceptance_criteria: Allocator produces deterministic fractional allocations for identical input event order (idempotency across replays)
End-to-end test harness demonstrates >60% reduction in retro-credit volume for synthetic multi-route workloads compared to baseline (stat sig over 20 runs)
Allocator outputs compact attribution events (JSON schema v2) and writes to topic billing.attribution.v2 with production throughput 10k events/s and <200ms p95 processing latency
All edge cases for late-arrival tokens (window TTLs, out-of-order replays) are covered and documented
Console tracing link for each allocation contains explainability fields (weight components and confidence score)

2026-03-04 - Maya Patel (PM): Requested explicit explainability fields for auditability; added weight breakdown (route_score, latency_score, historical_share) to event schema.

2026-03-11 - Diego Morales: Opened PR for microservice wrapper and Beam transform: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/11234 (WIP). Added unit tests for idempotency and replay behavior.

decisions: Use Beam streaming transform (Dataflow runner) for initial rollout to leverage existing streaming infra (decision 2026-02-18)
Adopt bounded per-session state with 5-minute sliding window and 24-hour tombstone TTL to balance memory and late-arrival coverage (decision 2026-02-25)
Emit attribution as fractional token allocations with decimal precision 1e-4; downstream ledger will round per business rules during invoice aggregation (decision 2026-03-03)
Shadow-run for 48-72h then staggered canary across low-risk tenants before full write enablement (decision 2026-03-07)
open_questions: What tenant tiers require stricter determinism vs probabilistic smoothing? (affects policy override)
Do we need to surface individual allocation adjustments to customers or only final invoice-level summaries? (billing UX dependency)
Edge case: how to handle sessions that span >24 hours—should we increase TTL for specific enterprise tenants?
Confirm required retention period for explainability traces for audit/compliance (legal needs to advise)
